sources.name: NASA/JPL Sentry: Earth Impact Monitoring
sources.description: Automated collision monitoring system continuously scanning asteroid orbits for potential Earth impacts over next 100+ years.

sources.name: NASA/JPL Close Approach Data (CAD) API
sources.description: High-precision geometric close approaches of NEAs to Earth, including approach date, miss distance (AU / Lunar Distances), and relative velocity (km/s).

authoritative_target_definition: NASA/JPL defines a Potentially Hazardous Asteroid (PHA) based on two strict physical/orbital criteria: 1) Earth Minimum Orbit Intersection Distance (MOID) <= 0.05 AU (approx 19.5 Lunar Distances, ~7.48 million km); and 2) Absolute magnitude H <= 22.0, corresponding roughly to a diameter of >= 140 meters.
dataset_limitations: 1. Physical diameters are directly measured for only ~15% of asteroids (radar/WISE); the remainder are photometrically estimated from H assuming mean albedo p_v=0.14. 2. Asteroid orbits evolve under gravitational perturbations from planets and Yarkovsky thermal radiation drift. 3. Machine learning models predict PHA category membership based on orbital-physical geometry, but definitive impact risk requires numerical N-body orbit propagation and covariance propagation as performed by NASA Sentry.
